title: Cell-free reconstitution of peroxisomal matrix protein import using Xenopus egg extract
protocol: Induce ovulation by injecting 500 units of human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) into the dorsal lymph sacs of each primed frog using a fine 27-gauge hypodermic needle and sterile 1-mL syringe.
Discard used needles in an appropriate sharps-collection container.
Transfer each frog into 2 L of 1× MMR buffer.
House frogs overnight at 16°C in separate containers.
Do not maintain frogs in MMR buffer for longer than 16 hours to avoid osmotic stress.
Transfer frogs to a new container filled with conditioned water the following morning.
Allow frogs to complete ovulation for an additional 24 hours at 16°C.
Discard any additional eggs laid during the 24-hour period.
Allow frogs to recover for 3-4 months before reusing them for ovulation.
Carefully decant the eggs into a round glass dish.
Examine the eggs and remove any that look malformed or damaged using a 2-mL transfer pipet.
Decant most of the buffer from the glass dish, leaving some to cover the eggs.
Pour in one-third of the dejellying solution and gently swirl the dish for 1–2 minutes.
Decant most of the buffer again and add another third of the dejellying solution.
Gently swirl the dish for 1–2 minutes after adding the second portion.
Decant most of the buffer and pour in the final one-third of the dejellying solution.
Swirl the dish for 10–15 minutes or until the eggs have shed their jelly coats.
Decant most of the buffer.
Pour in 200 mL of XBS buffer and swirl for 2 min.
Decant most of the buffer, and repeat three more times with additional XBS buffer.
Pour in the last 200 mL of XBS buffer.
Cut the tip off a 2-mL soft polypropylene transfer pipet.
Tilt the dish and collect the eggs along one side.
Carefully scoop up some eggs using the prepared pipet and deposit in the tube, ensuring the pipet is immersed in buffer before expelling the eggs.
Repeat until the tube is almost completely full with eggs.
Aspirate off most of the buffer covering the eggs.
Centrifuge the tube at 16°C, first at 350 × g for 1 min, then at 1,200 × g for an additional minute.
Crush the eggs: Aspirate off as much residual buffer as possible, taking care not to disrupt the packed eggs.
Estimate the volume of packed eggs and add an appropriate volume of the 1000× stock solution of protease inhibitors, cytochalasin, and cycloheximide.
Centrifuge the tubes in an SW 55 Ti swinging-bucket rotor for 15 min at 12,100 × g and 16°C.
Place the centrifuged tubes on ice.
Isolate the cytoplasmic fraction.
Wipe one side of the tube with a kimwipe soaked in 100% ethanol.
Pierce the cleaned side of the tube with an 18-gauge beveled needle connected to a 1-mL syringe, just above the dark pellet on the bottom of the tube.
Prop the tube vertically against the side of the bench for easier piercing.
Ensure the needle is oriented with the beveled side facing up toward the cytoplasmic fraction.
Aspirate out the cytoplasmic layer by gently sweeping the needle from side to side while slowly pulling back the plunger.
Ensure that the rate fills a 1-mL syringe in 40–60 seconds to avoid disrupting organelles.
Expel the contents of the syringe into a microfuge tube on ice slowly.
Use a clean needle and syringe for each tube to prevent shearing of organelles by repeated sliding of the plunger.
Discard used needles in an appropriate sharps-collection container.
Add an appropriate volume of the 1000× stock solution of protease inhibitors, cytochalasin, and cycloheximide to each microfuge tube.
Mix the contents of the microfuge tubes by inversion.
Collect the extract on the bottom of the tube using a touchspin centrifuge.
Keep the collected extract on ice.
Gently vortex the prepared 1:1 suspension of protein-conjugated agarose beads.
Transfer 20 μL of the bead suspension (i.e., 10 μL of beads) using a wide-bore pipette tip to a 0.5-mL microfuge tube on ice.
Mark the desired volume on the outside of the tube as a reference when working with small volumes of beads.
Add 500 μL of cold XBH buffer to the tube.
Invert the tube a few times to mix.
Collect the beads by centrifugation for 1 min at 1,500 × g and 4°C.
Aspirate off the supernatant.
Repeat washing two more times.
Briefly spin the tube on a touchspin centrifuge to collect residual buffer on the bottom of the tube.
Completely aspirate off the remaining supernatant.
Add 200 μL of egg extract using a wide-bore pipette tip.
Press the pipette plunger past the first stop and aspirate up a larger volume of extract than intended for reverse pipetting.
Expel the actual volume by pressing on the plunger down to the first stop, ensuring no air is blown out.
Wipe excess extract off the outside of the pipette tip with a Kimwipe without touching the orifice.
Mix beads into the extract by gently swirling with a fine pipette tip.
Invert the tube a few times by hand and then rotate for 30 min at room temperature.
Briefly spin on a touchspin centrifuge to collect the extract on the bottom of the tube.
Transfer the mixture of extract and beads into a Micro-Spin column using a wide-bore pipette tip.
Partially cap the Micro-Spin column and briefly spin on a touchspin centrifuge to allow the egg extract to flow through while retaining the beads.
Ensure all of the extract has flowed through before proceeding.
Loosely cap the Micro-Spin column during centrifugation to avoid creating a vacuum.
Transfer PEX5-depleted egg extract to a microfuge tube using a wide-bore pipette tip.
Keep the transfered extract on ice.
Boil a small aliquot (e.g., 2 μL) of the PEX5-depleted extract in a 10-fold excess of Laemmli buffer according to conventional protocols.
Boil an equivalent aliquot of unmanipulated extract as a control.
Prepare serial two-fold dilutions of each sample.
Resolve samples by reducing sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) polyacrylamide-gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE).
Immunoblot for PEX5.
Estimate depletion efficiency from the resulting blot by densitometry.
Prepare three 0.2-mL tubes on ice.
Add reagents specified in the table (except GFP-SKL) to each tube.
Mix all components as per the order specified in the table, starting with egg extract.
Warm up the reaction mixtures briefly before adding cargo.
Add fluorescent cargo GFP-SKL to initiate import reactions.
Note: PEX5 may be used at higher concentrations (≤ 1 μM) to accelerate import.
Mix egg extract carefully by reverse pipetting to avoid air bubbles and ensure accuracy.
Transfer the egg extract using a wide-bore pipette tip to avoid shearing forces that could disrupt organelles.
Gently flick the tubes to mix, then collect the contents on the bottom of the tubes by briefly spinning them.
Pre-warm the tubes for 5 min at 24°C on a pre-heated thermoblock in a thermomixer or block heater.
Remove the tubes from the thermoblock and add fluorescent cargo to initiate import.
Gently flick the tubes to mix, then collect the contents by a brief touchspin.
Incubate the tubes in the thermoblock for 1 hour at 24°C.
Optional: Perform reactions at 16°C–18°C, closer to the frogs' physiological body temperature.
Note that egg extract becomes more viscous at lower temperatures and may be difficult to pipette.
Prepare egg extract for imaging.
Sandwich each import reaction between two passivated coverslips.
Mount the covered reactions on a slide using Valap sealant.
Incubate the samples to allow cargo import to continue linearly over time.
Optionally, spike each reaction with purified PEX5-binding domain from PEX14 at 10 μM concentration to stop further import.
Prepare coverslips by filling a clean container with 100% ethanol.
Heat the container containing ethanol to 100°C on a block heater or hot plate.
Submerge 3 passivated coverslip sandwiches in the heated ethanol bath and incubate for 5-10 minutes.
Remove a coverslip sandwich from the ethanol using fine-tipped tweezers.
Gently separate the coverslips using a clean razor blade.
Place the separated coverslips on a coverslip rack with PEGylated surfaces oriented in the same direction.
Rinse the coverslips well with 100% ethanol.
Remove residual PEG from coverslips using 100% ethanol rinse.
Rinse the coverslips extensively with ultrapure water.
Blow off excess water with compressed air or a handheld rubber bellows.
Place the rack on a hot plate warmed to 100°C until coverslips are dry.
Transfer the rack to a closed container to protect from dust.
Allow the coverslips to cool to RT.
Wipe 3 aluminum or glass slides with 100% ethanol to remove residual oils.
Blow off any dust from the slides.
Using fine-tipped tweezers, gently place a clean and dry passivated coverslip in the center of a slide with the PEGylated side facing up.
Mix the import reaction by gently flicking the tube.
Briefly spin down the tube on a touchspin centrifuge.
Pipette 10 μL of the import reaction onto the center of the coverslip.
Place a second coverslip on top of the sample to form a sandwich.
Ensure the passivated side of the second coverslip faces down toward the sample.
Lower the second coverslip at an angle from one side to minimize air bubbles.
Dab a little Valap sealant onto two corners of the assembled coverslip sandwich with a cotton swab.
Immerse the cotton swab in more Valap sealant and quickly shake off excess.
Smear the Valap along one side of the sandwich to form a seal.
Repeat for the remaining three sides to ensure complete sealing.
Dab any gaps or areas not properly sealed with additional Valap.
Label the slide with a marker.
Lay the labeled slide flat in a slide tray with coverslips facing up to protect from light.
Mount the first prepared slide in a slide holder on the microscope stage, with the coverslip side facing the objective.
Image the fluorescence of the reporter cargo (i.e., GFP-SKL) at multiple positions on the mounted slide.
Handle the slides gently.
Move the microscope stage slowly to avoid shaking the extract.
Configure the excitation light and optical elements in the microscope to be compatible with mEGFP fluorescence.
Bring the coverslip facing the objective into focus.
Adjust the focus to ∼5 μm above the coverslip (i.e., toward the middle of the sandwich).
Use an adaptive focusing system or manually adjust the focus if necessary.
Ensure that the objective is corrected for chromatic aberration and flat-field illumination.
Configure the acquisition software to image multiple fields arrayed around the center of the coverslip.
Reduce the stage speed to avoid shaking the extract during acquisition.
Adjust imaging parameters to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio while avoiding saturation of the camera.
Acquire images and repeat for the remaining samples.
Clean aluminum slides by heating on a hot plate to melt Valap sealant.
Scrape off the coverslip from heated slide.
Wipe off remaining sealant with a paper towel.
Clean residual grease by wiping with ethanol.
Discard used coverslips in an appropriate sharps-collection container.
